concepts.definition: The job of comparing generated text with the corpus to find the cause of the strangeness.
concepts.example: Looking up every pair of words in a generated sentence in the corpus and noting whether it is there or not.
concepts.pitfall: Just saying "it is silly"; the cause (copy, recombination, context) should be written down.

concepts.definition: The model produces a sentence from the corpus exactly as it is.
concepts.example: `öğretmen öğrenciye yardım eder .` (the teacher helps the student) also appears exactly in the mini corpus.
concepts.pitfall: Reading a copy as "the model understood and built a new sentence".

concepts.definition: Pieces that appear separately in the corpus come one after another in a new order that is not in the corpus.
concepts.example: `ileri gider ve` (goes forward and) and `ve engeli görür` (and sees the obstacle) each appear separately; the model can join them.
concepts.pitfall: Thinking the sentence will make sense because every pair of words is in the corpus.

concepts.definition: The model looks only at the last few words; it cannot see the start of the sentence or the whole of it.
concepts.example: A two-word context forgets the previous sentence after a full stop.
concepts.pitfall: Thinking of the strangeness as "the model made a mistake"; the limit is a natural result of the design.

concepts.term: The cost of a longer context
concepts.definition: A longer context makes the text more consistent, but it needs that context to appear often enough in the corpus, in other words more data.
concepts.example: Three-word contexts are often not found in a small corpus, and the model backs off.
concepts.pitfall: Thinking a longer context is always a free improvement.

quiz.prompt: In a sentence generated by the mini model, every pair of neighbouring words is in the corpus, but the sentence is meaningless. What is the most likely reason?
options: There is a spelling mistake in the corpus
The model lined up correct pairs one after another without checking the meaning of the whole
The tool asked a real model and got a wrong answer
quiz.explanation: At each step the model looks only at the last word (or two); even if the pairs are correct, the meaning of the whole is not checked. The seed picks the result but does not explain the meaninglessness; and the tool does not send a question to an outside model.

The generated sentence is not in the corpus list, so tam is false. But all three pairs, `robot sağa`, `sağa gider` and `gider .`, appear in one of the sentences in the corpus, so hepsiVar is true. This is the typical trace of recombination.

quiz.prompt: The starting word is "robot" and you had the tool generate 10 words. A full stop also counts as a word. There are 2 full stops in the output. How many words, including the start but not counting full stops, are in the text on the screen?
quiz.explanation: The start "robot" is 1 word; the tool generated 10 steps, 2 of which are full stops, so 8 are words. Not counting full stops, the total is 1 + 8 = 9. If you count the full stops too, you get 11.

quiz.prompt: What is the most important cost of using a three-word context?
options: More data is needed; otherwise the context is not found and the model backs off
quiz.explanation: A long context must have appeared word for word in the corpus; in a small corpus it often has not, and the model backs off to a shorter context. Speed or sentence length is not the real cost; the seed still works.

quiz.prompt: In the project you used "robot" with three different seeds and got three different sentences. Why are these three sentences different?
options: The seed changes the course of the random choice made according to the probabilities
The tool downloads a new model each time
All three sentences should have come out the same
quiz.explanation: The probabilities are the same; the seed is the start of the random sequence that decides which candidate is chosen. The corpus does not change and the tool downloads nothing from outside. The same seed would give the same sentence; a different seed opens a different path.
